after: ## How concepts work in an MYP unit
alt: The four key concepts for language acquisition are communication, connections, creativity and culture; the brief’s related-concept examples are word choice, conventions and idiom. Both are explored through the six global contexts. A topic such as food is not a concept; culture is a concept that applies to food, festivals and slang alike.
caption: Key concepts frame, related concepts ground, contexts give the setting.

alt: Communication has three checkable parts: audience, purpose and mode. The same cancellation becomes an informal spoken voicemail to a friend and a formal written email to a teacher. Statement of inquiry: the way we adapt our words to an audience shapes whether a message is understood and accepted.
caption: Same message, different audience: the language has to change.

alt: An informal complaint to a hotel, “Hey! Your room was rubbish and I want my cash back”, is rewritten for a formal audience: “Hey!” becomes “Dear Sir or Madam”, “rubbish” becomes “not of the standard advertised”, “cash back” becomes “a refund”, and a precise detail about the broken shower is added.
caption: Match words to the audience, then add precision.

alt: Four steps for an idiom met in a French blog: notice the literal meaning (“he put a rabbit on me”) makes no sense; use the context (the writer waited an hour at a café); infer the meaning (“he stood me up”); and record the idiom with its meaning and an example, not a literal translation.
caption: Idioms are decoded from context and learned as whole expressions.

after: ## Worked example: building a statement of inquiry
alt: For a unit on social media and friendship: choose the key concept communication, the related concepts conventions and word choice, and the global context identities and relationships; write the claim “The conventions of online communication shape how we build and keep friendships”; test that it transfers, is a claim and names no app; then add factual, conceptual and debatable questions.
caption: Concept + related concepts + context = one general, transferable claim.

after: ## How concepts work in an MYP unit
alt: Three question types in language acquisition: factual (how do you open a formal letter in Spanish?), conceptual (why do languages have different levels of politeness?) and debatable (should young people use slang in a job interview?). A question such as “How do people make friends online?” is an inquiry question, not a statement of inquiry.
caption: The curriculum explores all three kinds of question.
